title: Areshunk
summary: Areshunk is a Center Moriches placename for a neck of land and landing near the foot of Union Avenue. The name appears to preserve a corrupted form of Warishone, the name of an Unkechaug man associated with the neck.
address_label: Foot of Union Avenue, Center Moriches, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern waterfront point near the foot of Union Avenue, Center Moriches; not an exact deed boundary.
why_this_matters: Areshunk preserves a Center Moriches neck-and-landing name that records suggest may be connected to Warishone or Worishun, a Native personal or local name in the written record. That possibility matters because place names can preserve not only landforms, but also remembered people, families, and community presence. Even imperfect colonial records can point back to Native lives and relationships with specific shorelines.
introduction_content: Areshunk is identified as a neck of land at Centre Moriches in Brookhaven town. The same source notes that the landing at the foot of Union Avenue was sometimes called by this name, and later Unkechaug history connects the name with Worison or Warishone.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Arescunk, Aresunk, Warishone, and Worishun. Areshunk is interpreted as a corrupted form of Warishone, with a possible meaning of the forgetter. That interpretation remains tentative.

Why Place Names Matter

“The ancient “corn fields” are now covered with cedars, and the “chestnut trees” in the swamp have been burned for years, and the “burned woods” is merely a name.”

— William Wallace Tooker, The Indian Place-Names on Long Island and Islands Adjacent, with Their Probable Significations (1911), Printed p. xxiii; Internet Archive scan leaf n28
whereintheworld_content: Areshunk connects a named neck and landing with Warishone, an Unkechaug person remembered in deed records. Personal names, land records, and local geography are linked here within Long Island placename history.
